rationale: The assistant correctly identified the likely cause and specified the right lamp type ('25W, 230V heat-resistant glass bulb with an SES ... E14 cap', rated 'up to 300°C') for the known model, matching the hidden truth, and sensibly warned against a standard household bulb. Weaknesses: it only said 'Ensure the oven is switched off and cool' rather than isolating at the cooker switch, its steps skip removing the glass lens cover before unscrewing the bulb, it did not suggest reading the old bulb's rating to confirm, and it gave no fallback (lamp holder/wiring, engineer) if the new bulb fails. No fabrication, unsafe instruction or unjustified part; a homeowner would be reasonably well served despite the thin procedure.
